description: Every tool POST /mcp offers. Written by scripts/api_docs.sh from the registered tools; do not edit by hand. A key sees the tools its role allows (adminOnly ones need an admin key), and a tool whose feature is switched off answers like one that does not exist. route is the HTTP route the tool stands for, with the same rules; http_only are the routes a key may call that have no tool, and why.

http_only.reason: The MCP reference itself; tools/list gives the same list.
The API reference itself; GET /api/mcp.json is the MCP one.
File bytes: MCP messages are JSON, and clients cap their size. files_start_upload says where to send each piece, with the same key.
Ends a browser session; a key has none to end.
The browser's own activity reports (track.js), not an action.

tools.description: A link that signs your own account in on a browser or another device. Only a key with your account's full role may ask: one scoped down to user on an admin account is refused. Answers with login_url (open it to sign in; it works once unless max_uses says otherwise), expires_at and max_uses. Any older link the account could still use stops working; its signed-in devices stay signed in. Revoking or deleting this API key voids the link while it is unused, and signs out every device it signed in.

expires_in_minutes.description: 0 never expires. Default auth.login_token_ttl_seconds for a link that works once, auth.multi_use_login_token_ttl_seconds otherwise.

max_uses.description: Sign-ins the link allows: 1-1000, or 0 for unlimited. Default 1.

tools.title: A login link for yourself

annotations.title: Stop your own login link working

tools.description: Void your account's live login link without making a new one. Devices it already signed in stay signed in. Answers with removed: 0 or 1.
tools.name: cancel_my_login_link
tools.title: Stop your own login link working

tools.description: Make a new account and its first login link, to hand to the person. role is admin or user. Answers with user_id and the link. Answers with login_url (open it to sign in; it works once unless max_uses says otherwise), expires_at and max_uses. Any older link the account could still use stops working; its signed-in devices stay signed in. Revoking or deleting this API key voids the link while it is unused, and signs out every device it signed in.

expires_in_minutes.description: 0 never expires. Default auth.login_token_ttl_seconds for a link that works once, auth.multi_use_login_token_ttl_seconds otherwise.

max_uses.description: Sign-ins the link allows: 1-1000, or 0 for unlimited. Default 1.

Any older link the account could still use stops working; its signed-in devices stay signed in. Revoking or deleting this API key voids the link while it is unused, and signs out every device it signed in.

expires_in_minutes.description: 0 never expires. Default auth.login_token_ttl_seconds for a link that works once, auth.multi_use_login_token_ttl_seconds otherwise.

max_uses.description: Sign-ins the link allows: 1-1000, or 0 for unlimited. Default 1.

tools.name: files_get

tools.description: Reserve room for a file and get where to send it. The bytes do not go through MCP: POST each piece of chunk_bytes bytes (the last may be shorter), in order from index 0, as the raw body (Content-Type: application/octet-stream) to chunk_url with {index} filled in and the same Authorization: Bearer header this MCP connection uses. curl is a shell recipe that does all of it. Then call files_finish_upload.

type.description: Shown in the list. Downloads are always application/octet-stream.

tools.description: Seal an upload once every piece has arrived; the file is then ready to download. Asked again, it answers the same. If pieces are missing it says how many arrived (received).
